title: Introduce Master Data Management for Customer Data
narrative: Customer data is currently fragmented across the billing, CRM, and field service platforms with no single authoritative record. We require a master data management capability to create a trusted, unified customer record. This will support the BUS-STR-001 customer-centric operating model and enable consistent data across all channels.

requirements.title: Single customer record
requirements.description: The system shall maintain exactly one authoritative customer record per customer identity across all integrated platforms.

requirements.title: Data quality
requirements.description: Customer master data must meet a minimum 98% completeness and accuracy threshold as measured by automated data quality checks.

narrative-validation.finding: Narrative clearly states the business driver and proposed direction.
narrative-validation.impact: Well-formed narratives allow analysis to produce higher-quality, intent-aligned findings.
narrative-validation.recommendation: Add a quantified target outcome to make success measurable.
narrative-validation.rationale: Measurable outcomes enable Strategy Alignment to assess impact against existing KPIs.

narrative-validation.finding: Requirements are expressed as outcomes. Testability could be strengthened.
narrative-validation.impact: Untestable requirements cannot be formally verified at acceptance, increasing scope-drift risk.
narrative-validation.recommendation: Restate each requirement using 'The system shall...' with a measurable acceptance criterion.
narrative-validation.rationale: ISO 29148 requires verifiable requirements. Acceptance criteria prevent ambiguity at delivery.

impact-assessment.finding: Change affects artefacts across at least one architecture domain. References in narrative are consistent with current baseline.
impact-assessment.impact: Changes of this scope require catalogue updates to maintain traceability from strategy to implementation.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Identify all artefacts requiring amendment before moving to Proposed.
impact-assessment.rationale: Explicit impact lists allow Referential Integrity to run comprehensively and catch gaps early.

impact-assessment.finding: No conflicts with currently accepted decisions. The proposed change is additive.
impact-assessment.impact: Low conflict risk reduces review overhead and increases acceptance likelihood.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Proceed to Referential Integrity. Monitor for conflicts if ADR-002 is accepted in the same cycle.
impact-assessment.rationale: Additive decisions not contradicting accepted ADRs are eligible for expedited review.

referential-integrity.finding: All artefact IDs referenced in the narrative exist in the current architecture baseline. No broken references.
referential-integrity.impact: Valid references ensure analysis steps can read cited artefacts and the record remains coherent after acceptance.
referential-integrity.recommendation: Confirm new artefact IDs follow the established naming convention.
referential-integrity.rationale: Consistent naming ensures tooling and queries can resolve references without manual intervention.

referential-integrity.finding: Scope constraint aligns with an existing artefact type. Artefact folder exists for the target client and version.
referential-integrity.impact: Scope alignment allows Principles and Guardrails checks to be correctly scoped without false positives.
referential-integrity.recommendation: Verify instance data in the scoped artefact is current before acceptance.
referential-integrity.rationale: Analysis quality degrades when scoped artefacts contain outdated instance data.

strategy-alignment.finding: Decision is consistent with BUS-STR-002 and BUS-STR-005. No conflicts with existing strategic statements.
strategy-alignment.impact: Strategy alignment increases executive sponsorship likelihood and reduces governance-block risk.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Reference specific BUS-STR entries in the narrative to make alignment explicit and auditable.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Explicit strategy traceability satisfies the Pickle traceability requirement and supports reporting.

strategy-alignment.finding: Decision supports BUS-STR-003 (decide with data) by introducing a structured, queryable architecture artefact.
strategy-alignment.impact: Decisions advancing multiple strategic objectives deliver compound value.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Add a target-outcome entry to the strategy catalogue reflecting this decision's contribution.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Updated strategy entries close the feedback loop between acceptance and strategic progress tracking.

principles-alignment.finding: Decision consistent with Logical-layer principles for the target domain. No vendor-neutrality violations detected.
principles-alignment.impact: Principles alignment means the decision passes guardrails review without requiring exceptions.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Confirm alignment with Physical-layer guardrails, particularly approved platform standards.
principles-alignment.rationale: Guardrails are non-negotiable. Validating before acceptance prevents costly rework at implementation.

principles-alignment.finding: Observability principle not explicitly addressed in narrative or requirements. Soft gap, not a blocker.
principles-alignment.impact: Decisions omitting observability requirements risk delivering capabilities that are hard to monitor.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Add a Non-Functional requirement: all components must expose health and telemetry endpoints.
principles-alignment.rationale: Observability is codified in Application Guardrails. Addressing it at decision stage is cheaper.

proponent-analysis.finding: Decision addresses a genuine capability gap consistent with the organisation's technology direction.
proponent-analysis.impact: Proceeding reduces risk accumulation in the affected domain and supports near-term business commitments.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Approve with a measurable target outcome and an observability requirement added.
proponent-analysis.rationale: The cost of both additions is negligible compared to the strategic value of the capability introduced.

proponent-analysis.finding: Decision has a clear delivery owner and is aligned to an existing funded programme. Implementation risk is low to medium.
proponent-analysis.impact: Funded, sponsored decisions are significantly more likely to be implemented successfully and on schedule.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Proceed to Accepted. Assign a delivery champion and schedule a post-implementation review in 90 days.
proponent-analysis.rationale: Post-implementation reviews close the feedback loop and update the architecture catalogue.

challenger-analysis.finding: Decision introduces a dependency on a capability not yet fully mature in this organisation.
challenger-analysis.impact: Immature capabilities increase delivery timeline risk and may require additional skills or tooling.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Include a risk-mitigation requirement covering capability assessment and a fallback position.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Documenting a fallback at decision time reduces the cost of pivoting and satisfies Guardrails risk management.

challenger-analysis.finding: Decision scope is broad and may introduce unintended coupling if implementation boundaries are not defined.
challenger-analysis.impact: Poorly bounded decisions create technical debt and complicate future changes in adjacent domains.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Add a constraint: implementation must not create direct dependencies between affected and adjacent domains.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Explicit boundary constraints are cheaper now than to refactor post-delivery.

history.notes: Decision raised to address fragmented customer data across billing, CRM and field service.
Narrative and requirements reviewed by data architecture team. Submitted for analysis.
